claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength near 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength around 855 MPa at approximately 1000 °C.
Replacing Hf with V produces the composition VMoTaTiZr while leaving Mo, Ta, Ti, and Zr unchanged.
Replacing Hf with V will reduce the alloy's density.
Replacing Hf with V will preserve the alloy's room-temperature strengthening mechanisms.
Replacing Hf with V will preserve the alloy's high-temperature strengthening mechanisms.
The V-substituted alloy will maintain a BCC solid-solution structure.
The V-substituted alloy will retain lattice-distortion effects associated with high strength.
V has a lower atomic mass than Hf.
Solid-solution strengthening and lattice-distortion strengthening are the core strengthening mechanisms in this alloy.
V has electronic characteristics sufficiently similar to Hf to support solid-solution formation in VMoTaTiZr.
Preservation of solid-solution and lattice-distortion strengthening will sustain yield strength at room temperature and 1000 °C.
VMoTaTiZr is predicted to have a density 8–15% lower than 10.21 g/cm³.
VMoTaTiZr is predicted to have room-temperature yield strength within approximately ±10% of 1600 MPa.
VMoTaTiZr is predicted to have yield strength at 1000 °C within approximately ±10% of 855 MPa.
Testing is restricted to quasi-static loading at room temperature and 1000 °C under protocols matched to the baseline.
Outside the stated temperature and loading boundaries, different deformation mechanisms may operate.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies complete Hf-to-V substitution to form VMoTaTiZr, whereas the experiment permits either partial or full substitution. A partially substituted alloy is a different, unspecified intervention and composition.
